card.intuition: A context pointer is a mention in one document that points to another, so the agent can pull it into the context window only when the task calls for it. A bare path is useless; a pointer needs a stable path and enough description for the agent to know when following it is worth it.
card.analogy: A book's table of contents entry: one line that says where to find the appendix, saving you from reading all two thousand pages up front.
card.time_complexity: O(1 line per pointer in context): a pointer is one line in the context window, while the document behind it might be thousands of tokens that cost nothing until followed.
card.space_complexity: O(pointer + lazily loaded body): leave the body behind the pointer and only load it on demand, keeping the finite context window for the always-on rules.
when_to_use: When AGENTS.md is getting huge and most of it should be context pointers instead of content
When a task can be described concretely so the pointer matches how tasks present, like release, deploy, or rollback
When tying a secondary source back to the primary source it was derived from so lossiness is recoverable
When writing skill descriptions where the harness loads the description but the body waits behind the pointer
gotchas: A pointer needs a stable path and a description — a bare path gives the agent no reason to follow it and gets skipped
Keep always-on rules inline; only turn the deploy runbook and style guide into pointed-to skills
Avoid the word reference (too dry) and portal (too florid) when naming the concept

steps.label: Describe
steps.annotation: The pointer line states the stable path and enough description for the agent to know when following it is worth it.

steps.label: Match
steps.annotation: The agent sees the pointer text align with the current task and decides to follow it.

steps.label: Follow
steps.annotation: The agent makes a tool call to load the pointed-to document into the context window.

steps.label: Use
steps.annotation: Only the sessions or tasks that need the document ever pay for its tokens.

exercise.prompt: Write a function that builds a context pointer line: inline the topic when always loaded, otherwise point at the path with a task description.
hints: The pointer needs a stable path and a description of when to follow it
Join the path and description with a connector that reads like a task trigger
exercise.test_code:
assert make_pointer('internal/deploy.md', 'deploying', False) == 'pointer:see internal/deploy.md when deploying'
assert make_pointer('internal/deploy.md', 'deploying', True) == 'inline:deploying'
print('PASS')
